class.name: CgameDynamicCarver
class.brief_description: Budgeted dynamic obstacle carving over tiled walkable polygons, integrated with [NavigationServer3D] obstacles and bake carving.
class.description: [CgameDynamicCarver] keeps a grid of tiles, each holding convex walkable polygons in the X/Z plane (polygons are [Vector2] with X and Z). Obstacles (polygons or circles, grown by the agent radius) are subtracted from the tiles they touch. Adding or removing an obstacle only marks tiles as dirty; [method update] re-carves a limited number of them per call, which spreads the cost over frames like a tile cache. Re-carved tiles are reported through [method consume_changed_tiles] so that AI can repath, and [method path_affected] tells whether a path crosses a changed tile. Obstacle shapes are either a [PackedVector2Array] polygon or a [Dictionary] [code]{"center": Vector2, "radius": float, "segments": int}[/code]. Engine integration: - [method set_server_map] mirrors obstacles as [NavigationServer3D] obstacles for avoidance. - [method export_obstructions] adds obstacles as carving projected obstructions to a [NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData3D], exactly like a [NavigationObstacle3D] with [member NavigationObstacle3D.affect_navigation_mesh] and [member NavigationObstacle3D.carve_navigation_mesh], so a native tile rebake removes them from the baked mesh. - [method set_rebake_callable] is invoked for every tile re-carved, which is the place to queue a native tile rebake under the same per-call budget. [codeblock] var carver := CgameDynamicCarver.new() carver.setup(Rect2(0, 0, 200, 200), 20.0, 0.5) carver.add_obstacle("barricade", PackedVector2Array([Vector2(50, 50), Vector2(60, 50), Vector2(60, 70), Vector2(50, 70)])) func _physics_process(_delta): if carver.update(4) > 0: for tile in carver.consume_changed_tiles(): repath_agents_in(tile) [/codeblock]

method.name: add_obstacle
method.description: Adds an obstacle identified by [param id], replacing an existing obstacle with the same id. The tiles it touches are queued for re-carving. Shapes with fewer than 3 vertices are ignored.

method.name: consume_changed_tiles
method.description: Returns the tiles re-carved since the last call and clears the list.

method.name: export_obstructions
method.description: Adds the carvers of every obstacle (those intersecting [param rect] when it has an area) to [param source_geometry] as projected obstructions with carving enabled and returns how many were added.

method.name: find_path
method.description: Searches the carved polygons with A* and pulls the result straight with the funnel algorithm. Returns an empty array when either point is blocked or the destination is unreachable.

method.name: get_agent_radius
method.description: Returns the agent radius obstacles are grown by.

method.name: get_bounds
method.description: Returns the area covered by the tile grid.

method.name: get_obstacle_count
method.description: Returns the number of registered obstacles.

method.name: get_rebake_callable
method.description: Returns the callable set by [method set_rebake_callable].

method.name: get_server_map
method.description: Returns the [NavigationServer3D] map obstacles are mirrored on, or an invalid [RID].

method.name: get_server_obstacle_count
method.description: Returns how many obstacles currently have a [NavigationServer3D] obstacle.

method.name: get_tile_size
method.description: Returns the tile edge length.

method.name: get_tiles_rebuilt_total
method.description: Returns how many tiles were re-carved since [method setup] or [method set_walkable].

method.name: get_version
method.description: Returns a counter that increases for every [method update] call that re-carved at least one tile.

method.name: has_obstacle
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if an obstacle with [param id] exists.

method.name: is_convex
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param polygon] is convex (collinear vertices are tolerated).

method.name: is_walkable
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param point] lies on (or on the border of) a carved walkable polygon. Pending changes are not reflected until [method update] ran.

method.name: on_destroyed
method.description: Destruction hook: the obstacle stops blocking the navigation. Equivalent to [method remove_obstacle].

method.name: path_affected
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if any segment of [param path] passes through one of the [param changed] tiles.

method.name: pending_tiles
method.description: Returns how many tiles wait to be re-carved.

method.name: polygons_in_tile
method.description: Returns the convex walkable polygons of [param tile] as of the last re-carving.

method.name: remove_obstacle
method.description: Removes an obstacle and queues the tiles it touched. Returns [code]false[/code] if the id is unknown.

method.name: set_rebake_callable
method.description: Sets a callable invoked as [code]callable(tile: Vector2i, tile_rect: Rect2)[/code] for every tile re-carved by [method update].

method.name: set_server_map
method.description: Mirrors all current and future obstacles as [NavigationServer3D] obstacles on [param map] at height [param y] with the given [param height]. Pass an invalid [RID] to stop. Nothing is created when the server is a dummy.

method.name: set_walkable
method.description: Restricts walkable space to the given polygons (an array of [PackedVector2Array]) clipped into the tiles and re-carves everything.

method.name: setup
method.description: Creates a fully walkable tile grid covering [param bounds]. Existing obstacles are kept and applied. [param tile_size] is at least 1 and [param agent_radius] at least 0.

method.name: tile_count
method.description: Returns the grid size in tiles.

method.name: tile_of
method.description: Returns the tile containing [param point]. May be outside the grid.

method.name: tile_version
method.description: Returns how often [param tile] was re-carved since the grid was set up.

method.name: update
method.description: Re-carves up to [param max_tiles_per_call] dirty tiles (all of them when it is 0 or less) and returns how many were rebuilt.
